description: Tacos al Pastor are a vibrant Mexican street food classic, featuring thinly sliced pork marinated in a rich blend of chiles and spices, then stacked and spit-grilled with a crown of pineapple. The slow rotation on the vertical spit, or trompo, creates incredibly tender, flavorful meat with crispy edges, ready to be carved into warm tortillas. Each bite offers a perfect balance of savory, sweet, and spicy, making it an unforgettable culinary experience.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chiles
instructions.text: Rehydrate the dried ancho and guajillo chiles by soaking them in hot water for 20 minutes until softened. Drain and remove any remaining seeds or stems.

instructions.title: Make the Marinade
instructions.text: In a blender, combine the rehydrated chiles, achiote paste, white vinegar, orange juice, garlic cloves, chopped onion, cumin, oregano, black pepper, and salt. Blend until completely smooth.

instructions.title: Marinate the Pork
instructions.text: Place the thinly sliced pork shoulder in a large bowl or a resealable bag. Pour the marinade over the pork, ensuring all pieces are well coated. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to penetrate.

instructions.title: Assemble the Trompo
instructions.text: Remove the pork from the marinade. Skewer the pineapple onto the bottom of your vertical spit. Layer the marinated pork slices onto the spit, pressing them together firmly to form a compact cone shape. Top with another slice of pineapple.

instructions.title: Spit Grill the Pork
instructions.text: Place the assembled spit on your vertical rotisserie grill. Cook over medium-high heat, allowing the pork to slowly rotate and cook for about 2-3 hours, or until the internal temperature reaches 145F (63C) and the outer layers are caramelized and crispy. Slice off the outer layers as they cook.

instructions.title: Slice and Serve
instructions.text: As the pork cooks, use a sharp knife to shave thin slices of the crispy, cooked meat directly from the spit onto a cutting board. Finely chop any pineapple that cooks with the meat. Serve the sliced al pastor on warm corn tortillas, topped with diced white onion, fresh cilantro, and a squeeze of lime. Add your favorite salsa for an extra kick.

tips: For a deeper flavor, toast the dried chiles in a dry pan for 1-2 minutes before rehydrating. Be careful not to burn them.

If you don't have a vertical spit, you can cook al pastor in a very hot oven (400F/200C) on a baking sheet lined with foil, turning occasionally, or on a flat top grill, chopping the meat as it cooks.
Always warm your corn tortillas before serving. A quick pass over an open flame, on a comal, or wrapped in a damp towel and microwaved will make them soft and pliable.
